anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-layer statements or transaction patterns that obligate the engine to scan or modify more data, rows, or duration than the true business need demands.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions compete for incompatible locks on the same resources, producing long blocking chains or deadlocks.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Allocated data, log, or temporary space is exhausted or nearly exhausted, preventing further allocations and blocking space-consuming operations.

When these three root causes coexist, the system experiences a compound failure mode: overly heavy or long-lived SQL requests inflate undo, redo, and temporary usage just as they hold locks for extended periods; meanwhile, shrinking free space slows or halts growth of data files, temp segments, and transaction logs. Observable effects include: 1) surging statement and transaction latency with frequent application timeouts, 2) expanding lock wait graphs where blockers cannot finish because they are stalled on space-allocation or log flush operations, 3) deadlocks followed by rollbacks that re-execute the same inefficient SQL, 4) rapid consumption of tablespace, log, or temp space culminating in allocation-failure errors that freeze active transactions mid-commit, and 5) escalating connection-pool saturation as sessions queue behind both locks and space shortages, making it difficult to isolate a single culprit.

Causally, chatty or scan-heavy SQL inflates row-level change sets and temp work files, which in turn intensify lock footprints and prolong transaction lifetimes. The prolonged holds amplify contention, increasing the number and duration of waiting transactions. Each blocked or retried transaction further multiplies DML volume and redo generation, accelerating consumption of data and log space. As space nears exhaustion, auto-extend or log-archive operations stall, preventing commit processing and keeping locks active even longer, which deepens the contention spiral. The feedback loop between space exhaustion, prolonged lock retention, and inefficient SQL processing can rapidly degrade OLTP throughput and force widespread rollbacks or outages.

entry.official_description: You can't execute a prepared statement which has an open cursor associated with it. Reset the statement to re-execute it.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
